html:
The Marinids were a Berber dynasty of the Zenata tribes who ruled Morocco from the mid 13th century to 1465. They are shown here in 1279, ten years after they took Marrakesh from the Almohads.

They made Fez their capital and built a new royal city beside it, Fes el-Jdid. Their lasting mark is the madrasas, colleges for religious study with carved wood and tile, such as the Bou Inania in Fez. They fought for decades with their neighbours, the Abd al-Wadids of Tlemcen, and the Hafsids of Tunis. Sultan Abu al-Hasan took Tlemcen in 1337 and Tunis in 1347, but he had lost to Castile and Portugal at the Battle of Río Salado in Spain in 1340, and his eastern conquests soon collapsed.

The traveller Ibn Battuta set out from Marinid Morocco and wrote up his journeys for a Marinid sultan. Ibn Khaldun served at their court. Their viziers, the Wattasids, took over in the 15th century.
